lines.text: Enter King Richard, John of Gaunt, with other Nobles and Attendants.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Old John of Gaunt, time-honoured Lancaster,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Hast thou, according to thy oath and band,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Brought hither Henry Hereford, thy bold son,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Here to make good the boist’rous late appeal,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Which then our leisure would not let us hear,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Against the Duke of Norfolk, Thomas Mowbray?

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: I have, my liege.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Tell me, moreover, hast thou sounded him

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: If he appeal the Duke on ancient malice,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Or worthily, as a good subject should,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: On some known ground of treachery in him?

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: As near as I could sift him on that argument,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: On some apparent danger seen in him

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Aimed at your Highness, no inveterate malice.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Then call them to our presence. Face to face

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And frowning brow to brow, ourselves will hear

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The accuser and the accused freely speak.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: High-stomached are they both and full of ire,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: In rage, deaf as the sea, hasty as fire.
Enter Bolingbroke and Mowbray.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Many years of happy days befall

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: My gracious sovereign, my most loving liege!

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Each day still better other’s happiness

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Until the heavens, envying earth’s good hap,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Add an immortal title to your crown!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: We thank you both. Yet one but flatters us,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: As well appeareth by the cause you come,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Namely, to appeal each other of high treason.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Cousin of Hereford, what dost thou object

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Against the Duke of Norfolk, Thomas Mowbray?

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: First—heaven be the record to my speech!—

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: In the devotion of a subject’s love,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Tend’ring the precious safety of my prince,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And free from other misbegotten hate,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Come I appellant to this princely presence.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Now, Thomas Mowbray, do I turn to thee,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And mark my greeting well; for what I speak

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: My body shall make good upon this earth,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Or my divine soul answer it in heaven.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Thou art a traitor and a miscreant,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Too good to be so and too bad to live,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Since the more fair and crystal is the sky,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: The uglier seem the clouds that in it fly.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Once more, the more to aggravate the note,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: With a foul traitor’s name stuff I thy throat,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And wish, so please my sovereign, ere I move,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: What my tongue speaks, my right-drawn sword may prove.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Let not my cold words here accuse my zeal.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: ’Tis not the trial of a woman’s war,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: The bitter clamour of two eager tongues,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Can arbitrate this cause betwixt us twain;

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: The blood is hot that must be cooled for this.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Yet can I not of such tame patience boast

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: As to be hushed and naught at all to say.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: First, the fair reverence of your highness curbs me

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: From giving reins and spurs to my free speech,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Which else would post until it had returned

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: These terms of treason doubled down his throat.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Setting aside his high blood’s royalty,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And let him be no kinsman to my liege,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: I do defy him, and I spit at him,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Call him a slanderous coward and a villain;

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Which to maintain, I would allow him odds

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And meet him, were I tied to run afoot

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Even to the frozen ridges of the Alps,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Or any other ground inhabitable

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Wherever Englishman durst set his foot.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Meantime let this defend my loyalty:

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: By all my hopes, most falsely doth he lie.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Pale trembling coward, there I throw my gage,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Disclaiming here the kindred of the King,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And lay aside my high blood’s royalty,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Which fear, not reverence, makes thee to except.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: If guilty dread have left thee so much strength

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: As to take up mine honour’s pawn, then stoop.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: By that and all the rites of knighthood else,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Will I make good against thee, arm to arm,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: What I have spoke or thou canst worst devise.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: I take it up; and by that sword I swear

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Which gently laid my knighthood on my shoulder,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: I’ll answer thee in any fair degree

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Or chivalrous design of knightly trial.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And when I mount, alive may I not light

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: If I be traitor or unjustly fight!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: What doth our cousin lay to Mowbray’s charge?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: It must be great that can inherit us

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: So much as of a thought of ill in him.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Look what I speak, my life shall prove it true:

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: That Mowbray hath received eight thousand nobles

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: In name of lendings for your highness’ soldiers,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: The which he hath detained for lewd employments,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Like a false traitor and injurious villain.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Besides I say, and will in battle prove,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Or here or elsewhere to the furthest verge

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: That ever was surveyed by English eye,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: That all the treasons for these eighteen years

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Complotted and contrived in this land

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Fetch from false Mowbray their first head and spring.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Further I say, and further will maintain

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Upon his bad life to make all this good,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: That he did plot the Duke of Gloucester’s death,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Suggest his soon-believing adversaries,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And consequently, like a traitor coward,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Sluiced out his innocent soul through streams of blood,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Which blood, like sacrificing Abel’s, cries

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Even from the tongueless caverns of the earth

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To me for justice and rough chastisement.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And, by the glorious worth of my descent,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: This arm shall do it, or this life be spent.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: How high a pitch his resolution soars!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Thomas of Norfolk, what sayst thou to this?

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: O! let my sovereign turn away his face

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And bid his ears a little while be deaf,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Till I have told this slander of his blood

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: How God and good men hate so foul a liar.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Mowbray, impartial are our eyes and ears.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Were he my brother, nay, my kingdom’s heir,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: As he is but my father’s brother’s son,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Now, by my sceptre’s awe I make a vow

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Such neighbour nearness to our sacred blood

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Should nothing privilege him nor partialize

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The unstooping firmness of my upright soul.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: He is our subject, Mowbray; so art thou.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Free speech and fearless I to thee allow.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Then, Bolingbroke, as low as to thy heart,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Through the false passage of thy throat, thou liest.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Three parts of that receipt I had for Calais

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Disbursed I duly to his highness’ soldiers;

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: The other part reserved I by consent,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: For that my sovereign liege was in my debt

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Upon remainder of a dear account

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Since last I went to France to fetch his queen.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Now swallow down that lie. For Gloucester’s death,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: I slew him not, but to my own disgrace

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Neglected my sworn duty in that case.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: For you, my noble Lord of Lancaster,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: The honourable father to my foe,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Once did I lay an ambush for your life,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: A trespass that doth vex my grieved soul;

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: But ere I last received the sacrament

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: I did confess it and exactly begged

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Your Grace’s pardon, and I hope I had it.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: This is my fault. As for the rest appealed,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: It issues from the rancour of a villain,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: A recreant and most degenerate traitor,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Which in myself I boldly will defend,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And interchangeably hurl down my gage

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Upon this overweening traitor’s foot,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: To prove myself a loyal gentleman

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Even in the best blood chambered in his bosom.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: In haste whereof most heartily I pray

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Your highness to assign our trial day.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Wrath-kindled gentlemen, be ruled by me.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Let’s purge this choler without letting blood.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: This we prescribe, though no physician;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Deep malice makes too deep incision.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Forget, forgive, conclude and be agreed;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Our doctors say this is no month to bleed.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Good uncle, let this end where it begun;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: We’ll calm the Duke of Norfolk, you your son.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: To be a make-peace shall become my age.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Throw down, my son, the Duke of Norfolk’s gage.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And, Norfolk, throw down his.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: When, Harry, when?

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Obedience bids I should not bid again.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Norfolk, throw down, we bid; there is no boot.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Myself I throw, dread sovereign, at thy foot.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: My life thou shalt command, but not my shame.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: The one my duty owes; but my fair name,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Despite of death that lives upon my grave,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: To dark dishonour’s use thou shalt not have.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: I am disgraced, impeached, and baffled here,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Pierced to the soul with slander’s venomed spear,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: The which no balm can cure but his heart-blood

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Which breathed this poison.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Rage must be withstood.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Give me his gage. Lions make leopards tame.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Yea, but not change his spots. Take but my shame,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And I resign my gage. My dear dear lord,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: The purest treasure mortal times afford

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Is spotless reputation; that away,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Men are but gilded loam or painted clay.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: A jewel in a ten-times-barred-up chest

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Is a bold spirit in a loyal breast.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Mine honour is my life; both grow in one.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Take honour from me, and my life is done.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Then, dear my liege, mine honour let me try;

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: In that I live, and for that will I die.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Cousin, throw up your gage; do you begin.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: O, God defend my soul from such deep sin!

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Shall I seem crest-fallen in my father’s sight?

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Or with pale beggar-fear impeach my height

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Before this outdared dastard? Ere my tongue

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Shall wound my honour with such feeble wrong

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Or sound so base a parle, my teeth shall tear

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: The slavish motive of recanting fear

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And spit it bleeding in his high disgrace,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Where shame doth harbour, even in Mowbray’s face.
[_Exit Gaunt._]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: We were not born to sue, but to command;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Which since we cannot do to make you friends,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Be ready, as your lives shall answer it,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: At Coventry upon Saint Lambert’s day.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: There shall your swords and lances arbitrate

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The swelling difference of your settled hate.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Since we cannot atone you, we shall see

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Justice design the victor’s chivalry.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Lord Marshal, command our officers-at-arms

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Be ready to direct these home alarms.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. A room in the Duke of Lancaster’s palace.

lines.text: Enter John of Gaunt with the Duchess of Gloucester.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Alas, the part I had in Woodstock’s blood

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Doth more solicit me than your exclaims

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: To stir against the butchers of his life.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: But since correction lieth in those hands

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Which made the fault that we cannot correct,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Put we our quarrel to the will of heaven,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Who, when they see the hours ripe on earth,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Will rain hot vengeance on offenders’ heads.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Finds brotherhood in thee no sharper spur?

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Hath love in thy old blood no living fire?

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Edward’s seven sons, whereof thyself art one,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Were as seven vials of his sacred blood,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Or seven fair branches springing from one root.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Some of those seven are dried by nature’s course,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Some of those branches by the Destinies cut;

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: But Thomas, my dear lord, my life, my Gloucester,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: One vial full of Edward’s sacred blood,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: One flourishing branch of his most royal root,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Is cracked, and all the precious liquor spilt,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Is hacked down, and his summer leaves all faded,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: By envy’s hand and murder’s bloody axe.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Ah, Gaunt! his blood was thine! That bed, that womb,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: That metal, that self mould, that fashioned thee

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Made him a man; and though thou livest and breathest,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Yet art thou slain in him. Thou dost consent

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: In some large measure to thy father’s death

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: In that thou seest thy wretched brother die,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Who was the model of thy father’s life.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Call it not patience, Gaunt; it is despair.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: In suff’ring thus thy brother to be slaughtered,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Thou showest the naked pathway to thy life,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Teaching stern murder how to butcher thee.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: That which in mean men we entitle patience

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Is pale cold cowardice in noble breasts.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: What shall I say? To safeguard thine own life,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: The best way is to venge my Gloucester’s death.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: God’s is the quarrel; for God’s substitute,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: His deputy anointed in His sight,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Hath caused his death, the which if wrongfully,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Let heaven revenge, for I may never lift

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: An angry arm against His minister.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Where then, alas! may I complain myself?

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: To God, the widow’s champion and defence.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Why then, I will. Farewell, old Gaunt.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Thou goest to Coventry, there to behold

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Our cousin Hereford and fell Mowbray fight.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: O, sit my husband’s wrongs on Hereford’s spear,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: That it may enter butcher Mowbray’s breast!

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Or if misfortune miss the first career,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Be Mowbray’s sins so heavy in his bosom

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: That they may break his foaming courser’s back

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: And throw the rider headlong in the lists,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: A caitiff recreant to my cousin Hereford!

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Farewell, old Gaunt. Thy sometimes brother’s wife

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: With her companion, Grief, must end her life.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Sister, farewell; I must to Coventry.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: As much good stay with thee as go with me!

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Yet one word more. Grief boundeth where it falls,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Not with the empty hollowness, but weight.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: I take my leave before I have begun,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: For sorrow ends not when it seemeth done.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Commend me to thy brother, Edmund York.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Lo, this is all. Nay, yet depart not so!

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Though this be all, do not so quickly go;

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: I shall remember more. Bid him—ah, what?—

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: With all good speed at Plashy visit me.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Alack, and what shall good old York there see

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: But empty lodgings and unfurnished walls,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Unpeopled offices, untrodden stones?

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: And what hear there for welcome but my groans?

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Therefore commend me; let him not come there

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: To seek out sorrow that dwells everywhere.

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Desolate, desolate, will I hence and die!

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: The last leave of thee takes my weeping eye.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Open Space, near Coventry. Lists set out, and a Throne.

lines.text: Heralds, &c., attending.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Yea, at all points, and longs to enter in.

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: The Duke of Norfolk, sprightfully and bold,

lines.text: Stays but the summons of the appelant’s trumpet.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Why then, the champions are prepared and stay

lines.text: For nothing but his Majesty’s approach.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Marshal, demand of yonder champion

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The cause of his arrival here in arms.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Ask him his name, and orderly proceed

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To swear him in the justice of his cause.

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: In God’s name and the King’s, say who thou art,

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: And why thou comest thus knightly clad in arms,

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: Against what man thou com’st, and what thy quarrel.

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: Speak truly, on thy knighthood and thy oath,

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: As so defend thee heaven and thy valour.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: My name is Thomas Mowbray, Duke of Norfolk,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Who hither come engaged by my oath—

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Which God defend a knight should violate!—

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Both to defend my loyalty and truth

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: To God, my King, and my succeeding issue,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Against the Duke of Hereford that appeals me,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And, by the grace of God and this mine arm,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: To prove him, in defending of myself,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: A traitor to my God, my king, and me;

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And as I truly fight, defend me heaven.
[_He takes his seat._]

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Trumpet sounds. Enter Bolingbroke, appellant, in armour, preceded by

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: a Herald.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Marshal, ask yonder knight in arms

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Both who he is and why he cometh hither

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Thus plated in habiliments of war,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And formally, according to our law,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Depose him in the justice of his cause.

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: What is thy name? And wherefore com’st thou hither

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: Before King Richard in his royal lists?

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: Against whom comest thou? and what’s thy quarrel?

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: Speak like a true knight, so defend thee heaven!

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Harry of Hereford, Lancaster, and Derby,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Am I, who ready here do stand in arms

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To prove by God’s grace and my body’s valour,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: In lists, on Thomas Mowbray, Duke of Norfolk,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: That he’s a traitor foul and dangerous,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To God of heaven, King Richard, and to me.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And as I truly fight, defend me heaven.

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: On pain of death, no person be so bold

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: Or daring-hardy as to touch the lists,

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: Except the Marshal and such officers

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: Appointed to direct these fair designs.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Lord Marshal, let me kiss my sovereign’s hand

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And bow my knee before his Majesty.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: For Mowbray and myself are like two men

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: That vow a long and weary pilgrimage;

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Then let us take a ceremonious leave

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And loving farewell of our several friends.

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: The appellant in all duty greets your highness

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: And craves to kiss your hand and take his leave.
[_Descends from his throne_.]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: We will descend and fold him in our arms.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Cousin of Hereford, as thy cause is right,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: So be thy fortune in this royal fight.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Farewell, my blood, which if today thou shed,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Lament we may, but not revenge thee dead.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: O, let no noble eye profane a tear

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: For me, if I be gored with Mowbray’s spear.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: As confident as is the falcon’s flight

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Against a bird, do I with Mowbray fight.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: My loving lord, I take my leave of you.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Of you, my noble cousin, Lord Aumerle;

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Not sick, although I have to do with death,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: But lusty, young, and cheerly drawing breath.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Lo! as at English feasts, so I regreet

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: The daintiest last, to make the end most sweet.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: O thou, the earthly author of my blood,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Whose youthful spirit, in me regenerate,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Doth with a twofold vigour lift me up

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To reach at victory above my head,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Add proof unto mine armour with thy prayers,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And with thy blessings steel my lance’s point,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: That it may enter Mowbray’s waxen coat

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And furbish new the name of John o’ Gaunt,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Even in the lusty haviour of his son.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: God in thy good cause make thee prosperous.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Be swift like lightning in the execution,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: And let thy blows, doubly redoubled,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Fall like amazing thunder on the casque

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Of thy adverse pernicious enemy.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Rouse up thy youthful blood, be valiant, and live.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Mine innocence and Saint George to thrive!
[_He takes his seat._]
[_Rising_.]

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: However God or fortune cast my lot,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: There lives or dies, true to King Richard’s throne,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: A loyal, just, and upright gentleman.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Never did captive with a freer heart

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Cast off his chains of bondage and embrace

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: His golden uncontrolled enfranchisement,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: More than my dancing soul doth celebrate

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: This feast of battle with mine adversary.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Most mighty liege, and my companion peers,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Take from my mouth the wish of happy years.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: As gentle and as jocund as to jest

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Go I to fight. Truth hath a quiet breast.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Farewell, my lord. Securely I espy

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Virtue with valour couched in thine eye.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Order the trial, Marshal, and begin.
[_The King and the Lords return to their seats._]

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: Harry of Hereford, Lancaster, and Derby,

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: Receive thy lance; and God defend the right.
[_Rising_.]

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Strong as a tower in hope, I cry “Amen”!
[_To an officer_.]

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: Go bear this lance to Thomas, Duke of Norfolk.

lines.speaker: FIRST HERALD
lines.text: Harry of Hereford, Lancaster, and Derby,

lines.speaker: FIRST HERALD
lines.text: Stands here for God, his sovereign, and himself,

lines.speaker: FIRST HERALD
lines.text: On pain to be found false and recreant,

lines.speaker: FIRST HERALD
lines.text: To prove the Duke of Norfolk, Thomas Mowbray,

lines.speaker: FIRST HERALD
lines.text: A traitor to his God, his King, and him,

lines.speaker: FIRST HERALD
lines.text: And dares him to set forward to the fight.

lines.speaker: SECOND HERALD
lines.text: Here standeth Thomas Mowbray, Duke of Norfolk,

lines.speaker: SECOND HERALD
lines.text: On pain to be found false and recreant,

lines.speaker: SECOND HERALD
lines.text: Both to defend himself and to approve

lines.speaker: SECOND HERALD
lines.text: Henry of Hereford, Lancaster, and Derby,

lines.speaker: SECOND HERALD
lines.text: To God, his sovereign, and to him disloyal,

lines.speaker: SECOND HERALD
lines.text: Courageously and with a free desire,

lines.speaker: SECOND HERALD
lines.text: Attending but the signal to begin.

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: Sound trumpets, and set forward, combatants.
[_A charge sounded._]

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: Stay! the King hath thrown his warder down.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Let them lay by their helmets and their spears,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And both return back to their chairs again.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Withdraw with us, and let the trumpets sound

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: While we return these dukes what we decree.
[_A long flourish._]
[_To the Combatants_.]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Draw near,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And list what with our council we have done.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: For that our kingdom’s earth should not be soiled

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: With that dear blood which it hath fostered;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And for our eyes do hate the dire aspect

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Of civil wounds ploughed up with neighbours’ swords;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And for we think the eagle-winged pride

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Of sky-aspiring and ambitious thoughts,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: With rival-hating envy, set on you

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To wake our peace, which in our country’s cradle

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Draws the sweet infant breath of gentle sleep,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Which so roused up with boist’rous untuned drums,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: With harsh-resounding trumpets’ dreadful bray,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And grating shock of wrathful iron arms,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Might from our quiet confines fright fair peace

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And make us wade even in our kindred’s blood:

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Therefore we banish you our territories.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: You, cousin Hereford, upon pain of life,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Till twice five summers have enriched our fields

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Shall not regreet our fair dominions,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: But tread the stranger paths of banishment.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Your will be done. This must my comfort be:

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: That sun that warms you here shall shine on me,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And those his golden beams to you here lent

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Shall point on me and gild my banishment.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Norfolk, for thee remains a heavier doom,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Which I with some unwillingness pronounce:

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The sly slow hours shall not determinate

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The dateless limit of thy dear exile.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The hopeless word of “never to return”

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Breathe I against thee, upon pain of life.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: A heavy sentence, my most sovereign liege,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And all unlooked for from your highness’ mouth.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: A dearer merit, not so deep a maim

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: As to be cast forth in the common air,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Have I deserved at your highness’ hands.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: The language I have learnt these forty years,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: My native English, now I must forgo;

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And now my tongue’s use is to me no more

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Than an unstringed viol or a harp,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Or like a cunning instrument cased up

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Or, being open, put into his hands

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: That knows no touch to tune the harmony.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Within my mouth you have engaoled my tongue,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Doubly portcullised with my teeth and lips,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And dull unfeeling, barren ignorance

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Is made my gaoler to attend on me.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: I am too old to fawn upon a nurse,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Too far in years to be a pupil now.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: What is thy sentence, then, but speechless death,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Which robs my tongue from breathing native breath?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: It boots thee not to be compassionate.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: After our sentence plaining comes too late.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Then thus I turn me from my country’s light,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: To dwell in solemn shades of endless night.
[_Retiring._]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Return again, and take an oath with thee.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Lay on our royal sword your banished hands.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Swear by the duty that you owe to God—

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Our part therein we banish with yourselves—

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To keep the oath that we administer:

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: You never shall, so help you truth and God,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Embrace each other’s love in banishment;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Nor never look upon each other’s face;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Nor never write, regreet, nor reconcile

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: This louring tempest of your home-bred hate;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Nor never by advised purpose meet

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To plot, contrive, or complot any ill

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: ’Gainst us, our state, our subjects, or our land.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: I swear.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And I, to keep all this.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Norfolk, so far as to mine enemy:

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: By this time, had the King permitted us,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: One of our souls had wandered in the air,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Banished this frail sepulchre of our flesh,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: As now our flesh is banished from this land.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Confess thy treasons ere thou fly the realm.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Since thou hast far to go, bear not along

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: The clogging burden of a guilty soul.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: No, Bolingbroke. If ever I were traitor,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: My name be blotted from the book of life,

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And I from heaven banished as from hence!

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: But what thou art, God, thou, and I do know;

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: And all too soon, I fear, the King shall rue.

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Farewell, my liege. Now no way can I stray;

lines.speaker: MOWBRAY
lines.text: Save back to England, all the world’s my way.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Uncle, even in the glasses of thine eyes

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I see thy grieved heart. Thy sad aspect

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Hath from the number of his banished years

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Plucked four away. [_To Bolingbroke_.] Six frozen winters spent,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Return with welcome home from banishment.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: How long a time lies in one little word!

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Four lagging winters and four wanton springs

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: End in a word: such is the breath of kings.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: I thank my liege that in regard of me

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: He shortens four years of my son’s exile;

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: But little vantage shall I reap thereby,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: For, ere the six years that he hath to spend

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Can change their moons and bring their times about,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: My oil-dried lamp and time-bewasted light

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Shall be extinct with age and endless night;

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: My inch of taper will be burnt and done,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: And blindfold death not let me see my son.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Why, uncle, thou hast many years to live.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: But not a minute, king, that thou canst give.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Shorten my days thou canst with sullen sorrow,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: And pluck nights from me, but not lend a morrow.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Thou canst help time to furrow me with age,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: But stop no wrinkle in his pilgrimage;

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Thy word is current with him for my death,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: But dead, thy kingdom cannot buy my breath.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Thy son is banished upon good advice,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Whereto thy tongue a party-verdict gave.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Why at our justice seem’st thou then to lour?

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Things sweet to taste prove in digestion sour.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: You urged me as a judge, but I had rather

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: You would have bid me argue like a father.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: O, had it been a stranger, not my child,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: To smooth his fault I should have been more mild.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: A partial slander sought I to avoid,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: And in the sentence my own life destroyed.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Alas, I looked when some of you should say

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: I was too strict to make mine own away;

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: But you gave leave to my unwilling tongue

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Against my will to do myself this wrong.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Cousin, farewell, and, uncle, bid him so.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Six years we banish him, and he shall go.
[_Flourish. Exit King Richard and Train._]

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Cousin, farewell. What presence must not know,

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: From where you do remain let paper show.

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: My lord, no leave take I, for I will ride,

lines.speaker: MARSHAL
lines.text: As far as land will let me, by your side.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: O, to what purpose dost thou hoard thy words,

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: That thou return’st no greeting to thy friends?

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: I have too few to take my leave of you,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: When the tongue’s office should be prodigal

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To breathe the abundant dolour of the heart.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Thy grief is but thy absence for a time.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Joy absent, grief is present for that time.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: What is six winters? They are quickly gone.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To men in joy; but grief makes one hour ten.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Call it a travel that thou tak’st for pleasure.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: My heart will sigh when I miscall it so,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Which finds it an enforced pilgrimage.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: The sullen passage of thy weary steps

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Esteem as foil wherein thou art to set

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: The precious jewel of thy home return.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Nay, rather, every tedious stride I make

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Will but remember me what a deal of world

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: I wander from the jewels that I love.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Must I not serve a long apprenticehood

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To foreign passages, and in the end,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Having my freedom, boast of nothing else

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: But that I was a journeyman to grief?

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: All places that the eye of heaven visits

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Are to a wise man ports and happy havens.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Teach thy necessity to reason thus:

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: There is no virtue like necessity.

lines.speaker: GAUNT
lines.text: Think not the King did banish thee,
