lines.text: By his attorneys-general to sue

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: His livery, and deny his offered homage,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: You pluck a thousand dangers on your head,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: You lose a thousand well-disposed hearts,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And prick my tender patience to those thoughts

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Which honour and allegiance cannot think.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Think what you will, we seize into our hands

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: His plate, his goods, his money, and his lands.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I’ll not be by the while. My liege, farewell.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: What will ensue hereof there’s none can tell;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: But by bad courses may be understood

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: That their events can never fall out good.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Go, Bushy, to the Earl of Wiltshire straight.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Bid him repair to us to Ely House

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To see this business. Tomorrow next

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: We will for Ireland, and ’tis time, I trow.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And we create, in absence of ourself,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Our Uncle York Lord Governor of England,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: For he is just, and always loved us well.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Come on, our queen. Tomorrow must we part;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Be merry, for our time of stay is short.
[_Exeunt King, Queen, Bushy, Aumerle, Green and Bagot._]

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Well, lords, the Duke of Lancaster is dead.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: And living too, for now his son is Duke.

lines.speaker: WILLOUGHBY
lines.text: Barely in title, not in revenues.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Richly in both, if justice had her right.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: My heart is great, but it must break with silence

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Ere’t be disburdened with a liberal tongue.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Nay, speak thy mind, and let him ne’er speak more

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: That speaks thy words again to do thee harm!

lines.speaker: WILLOUGHBY
lines.text: Tends that thou wouldst speak to the Duke of Hereford?

lines.speaker: WILLOUGHBY
lines.text: If it be so, out with it boldly, man.

lines.speaker: WILLOUGHBY
lines.text: Quick is mine ear to hear of good towards him.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: No good at all that I can do for him,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Unless you call it good to pity him,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Bereft and gelded of his patrimony.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Now, afore God, ’tis shame such wrongs are borne

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: In him, a royal prince, and many moe

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Of noble blood in this declining land.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: The King is not himself, but basely led

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: By flatterers; and what they will inform,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Merely in hate ’gainst any of us all,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: That will the King severely prosecute

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: ’Gainst us, our lives, our children, and our heirs.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: The commons hath he pilled with grievous taxes,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: And quite lost their hearts. The nobles hath he fined

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: For ancient quarrels and quite lost their hearts.

lines.speaker: WILLOUGHBY
lines.text: And daily new exactions are devised,

lines.speaker: WILLOUGHBY
lines.text: As blanks, benevolences, and I wot not what.

lines.speaker: WILLOUGHBY
lines.text: But what, i’ God’s name, doth become of this?

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Wars hath not wasted it, for warred he hath not,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: But basely yielded upon compromise

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: That which his ancestors achieved with blows.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: More hath he spent in peace than they in wars.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: The Earl of Wiltshire hath the realm in farm.

lines.speaker: WILLOUGHBY
lines.text: The King’s grown bankrupt like a broken man.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Reproach and dissolution hangeth over him.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: He hath not money for these Irish wars,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: His burdenous taxations notwithstanding,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: But by the robbing of the banished Duke.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: His noble kinsman. Most degenerate king!

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: But, lords, we hear this fearful tempest sing,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Yet seek no shelter to avoid the storm;

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: We see the wind sit sore upon our sails,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And yet we strike not, but securely perish.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: We see the very wrack that we must suffer;

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: And unavoided is the danger now

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: For suffering so the causes of our wrack.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Not so. Even through the hollow eyes of death

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: I spy life peering; but I dare not say

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: How near the tidings of our comfort is.

lines.speaker: WILLOUGHBY
lines.text: Nay, let us share thy thoughts as thou dost ours.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Be confident to speak, Northumberland.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: We three are but thyself, and, speaking so,

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Thy words are but as thoughts. Therefore be bold.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Then thus: I have from Le Port Blanc, a bay

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: In Brittany, received intelligence

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: That Harry Duke of Hereford, Rainold Lord Cobham,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: That late broke from the Duke of Exeter,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: His brother, Archbishop late of Canterbury,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Sir Thomas Erpingham, Sir John Ramston,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Sir John Norbery, Sir Robert Waterton, and Francis Coint,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: All these well furnished by the Duke of Brittany

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: With eight tall ships, three thousand men of war,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Are making hither with all due expedience,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And shortly mean to touch our northern shore.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Perhaps they had ere this, but that they stay

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: The first departing of the king for Ireland.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: If then we shall shake off our slavish yoke,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Imp out our drooping country’s broken wing,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Redeem from broking pawn the blemished crown,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Wipe off the dust that hides our sceptre’s gilt,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And make high majesty look like itself,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Away with me in post to Ravenspurgh.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: But if you faint, as fearing to do so,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Stay and be secret, and myself will go.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: To horse, to horse! Urge doubts to them that fear.

lines.speaker: WILLOUGHBY
lines.text: Hold out my horse, and I will first be there.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The Same. A Room in the Castle.

lines.text: Enter Queen, Bushy and Bagot.

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Madam, your Majesty is too much sad.

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: You promised, when you parted with the King,

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: To lay aside life-harming heaviness

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: And entertain a cheerful disposition.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: To please the King I did; to please myself

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: I cannot do it. Yet I know no cause

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Why I should welcome such a guest as grief,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Save bidding farewell to so sweet a guest

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: As my sweet Richard. Yet again methinks,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Some unborn sorrow, ripe in Fortune’s womb,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Is coming towards me, and my inward soul

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: With nothing trembles. At something it grieves

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: More than with parting from my lord the King.

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Each substance of a grief hath twenty shadows,

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Which shows like grief itself, but is not so;

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: For sorrow’s eye, glazed with blinding tears,

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Divides one thing entire to many objects,

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Like perspectives which, rightly gazed upon,

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Show nothing but confusion; eyed awry,

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Distinguish form. So your sweet Majesty,

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Looking awry upon your lord’s departure,

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Find shapes of grief more than himself to wail,

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Which, looked on as it is, is naught but shadows

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Of what it is not. Then, thrice-gracious Queen,

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: More than your lord’s departure weep not. More is not seen,

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Or if it be, ’tis with false sorrow’s eye,

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Which for things true weeps things imaginary.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: It may be so; but yet my inward soul

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Persuades me it is otherwise. Howe’er it be,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: I cannot but be sad—so heavy sad

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: As thought, in thinking, on no thought I think,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Makes me with heavy nothing faint and shrink.

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: ’Tis nothing but conceit, my gracious lady.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: ’Tis nothing less. Conceit is still derived

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: From some forefather grief. Mine is not so,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: For nothing hath begot my something grief,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Or something hath the nothing that I grieve.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: ’Tis in reversion that I do possess,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: But what it is, that is not yet known what,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: I cannot name. ’Tis nameless woe, I wot.
Enter Green.

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: God save your majesty! And well met, gentlemen.

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: I hope the King is not yet shipped for Ireland.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Why hop’st thou so? ’Tis better hope he is,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: For his designs crave haste, his haste good hope.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Then wherefore dost thou hope he is not shipped?

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: That he, our hope, might have retired his power,

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: And driven into despair an enemy’s hope

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: Who strongly hath set footing in this land.

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: The banished Bolingbroke repeals himself,

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: And with uplifted arms is safe arrived

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: At Ravenspurgh.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Now God in heaven forbid!

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: Ah, madam, ’tis too true; and that is worse,

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: The Lord Northumberland, his son young Harry Percy,

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: The Lords of Ross, Beaumond, and Willoughby,

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: With all their powerful friends, are fled to him.

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Why have you not proclaimed Northumberland

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: And all the rest revolted faction traitors?

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: We have, whereupon the Earl of Worcester

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: Hath broken his staff, resigned his stewardship,

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: And all the household servants fled with him

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: To Bolingbroke.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: So, Green, thou art the midwife to my woe,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And Bolingbroke my sorrow’s dismal heir.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Now hath my soul brought forth her prodigy,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And I, a gasping new-delivered mother,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Have woe to woe, sorrow to sorrow joined.

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Despair not, madam.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Who shall hinder me?

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: I will despair and be at enmity

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: With cozening hope. He is a flatterer,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: A parasite, a keeper-back of death,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Who gently would dissolve the bands of life,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Which false hope lingers in extremity.
Enter York.

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: Here comes the Duke of York.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: With signs of war about his aged neck.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: O! full of careful business are his looks!

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Uncle, for God’s sake, speak comfortable words.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Should I do so, I should belie my thoughts.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Comfort’s in heaven, and we are on the earth,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Where nothing lives but crosses, cares, and grief.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Your husband, he is gone to save far off,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Whilst others come to make him lose at home.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Here am I left to underprop his land,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Who, weak with age, cannot support myself.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Now comes the sick hour that his surfeit made;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Now shall he try his friends that flattered him.
Enter a Servingman.

lines.speaker: SERVINGMAN
lines.text: My lord, your son was gone before I came.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: He was? Why, so! Go all which way it will!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The nobles they are fled, the commons they are cold

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And will, I fear, revolt on Hereford’s side.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Sirrah, get thee to Plashy, to my sister Gloucester;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Bid her send me presently a thousand pound.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Hold, take my ring.

lines.speaker: SERVINGMAN
lines.text: My lord, I had forgot to tell your lordship:

lines.speaker: SERVINGMAN
lines.text: Today, as I came by, I called there—

lines.speaker: SERVINGMAN
lines.text: But I shall grieve you to report the rest.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: What is’t, knave?

lines.speaker: SERVINGMAN
lines.text: An hour before I came, the Duchess died.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: God for his mercy, what a tide of woes

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Comes rushing on this woeful land at once!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I know not what to do. I would to God,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: So my untruth had not provoked him to it,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The King had cut off my head with my brother’s.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: What, are there no posts dispatched for Ireland?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: How shall we do for money for these wars?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Come, sister—cousin, I would say, pray, pardon me.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Go, fellow, get thee home; provide some carts

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And bring away the armour that is there.
[_Exit Servingman._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Gentlemen, will you go muster men?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: If I know how or which way to order these affairs

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Thus disorderly thrust into my hands,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Never believe me. Both are my kinsmen.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Th’ one is my sovereign, whom both my oath

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And duty bids defend; th’ other again

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Is my kinsman, whom the King hath wronged,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Whom conscience and my kindred bids to right.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Well, somewhat we must do. Come, cousin,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I’ll dispose of you. Gentlemen, go muster up your men,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And meet me presently at Berkeley Castle.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I should to Plashy too,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: But time will not permit. All is uneven,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And everything is left at six and seven.
[_Exeunt York and Queen._]

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: The wind sits fair for news to go to Ireland,

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: But none returns. For us to levy power

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Proportionable to the enemy

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Is all unpossible.

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: Besides, our nearness to the King in love

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: Is near the hate of those love not the King.

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: And that is the wavering commons, for their love

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: Lies in their purses; and whoso empties them,

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: By so much fills their hearts with deadly hate.

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Wherein the King stands generally condemned.

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: If judgment lie in them, then so do we,

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: Because we ever have been near the King.

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: Well, I will for refuge straight to Bristol Castle.

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: The Earl of Wiltshire is already there.

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Thither will I with you, for little office

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Will the hateful commons perform for us,

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Except like curs to tear us all to pieces.

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Will you go along with us?

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: No, I will to Ireland to his Majesty.

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: Farewell. If heart’s presages be not vain,

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: We three here part that ne’er shall meet again.

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: That’s as York thrives to beat back Bolingbroke.

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: Alas, poor Duke! The task he undertakes

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: Is numb’ring sands and drinking oceans dry.

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: Where one on his side fights, thousands will fly.

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: Farewell at once, for once, for all, and ever.

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Well, we may meet again.

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: I fear me, never.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Bolingbroke and Northumberland with Forces.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: How far is it, my lord, to Berkeley now?

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Believe me, noble lord,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: I am a stranger here in Gloucestershire.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: These high wild hills and rough uneven ways

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Draws out our miles and makes them wearisome.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And yet your fair discourse hath been as sugar,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Making the hard way sweet and delectable.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: But I bethink me what a weary way

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: From Ravenspurgh to Cotshall will be found

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: In Ross and Willoughby, wanting your company,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Which, I protest, hath very much beguiled

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: The tediousness and process of my travel.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: But theirs is sweetened with the hope to have

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: The present benefit which I possess;

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And hope to joy is little less in joy

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Than hope enjoyed. By this the weary lords

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Shall make their way seem short as mine hath done

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: By sight of what I have, your noble company.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Of much less value is my company

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Than your good words. But who comes here?
Enter Harry Percy.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: It is my son, young Harry Percy,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Sent from my brother Worcester, whencesoever.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Harry, how fares your uncle?

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: I had thought, my lord, to have learned his health of you.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Why, is he not with the Queen?

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: No, my good lord. He hath forsook the court,

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: Broken his staff of office, and dispersed

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: The household of the King.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: What was his reason?

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: He was not so resolved when last we spake together.

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: Because your lordship was proclaimed traitor.

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: But he, my lord, is gone to Ravenspurgh

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: To offer service to the Duke of Hereford,

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: And sent me over by Berkeley to discover

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: What power the Duke of York had levied there,

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: Then with directions to repair to Ravenspurgh.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Have you forgot the Duke of Hereford, boy?

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: No, my good lord; for that is not forgot

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: Which ne’er I did remember. To my knowledge,

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: I never in my life did look on him.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Then learn to know him now. This is the Duke.

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: My gracious lord, I tender you my service,

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: Such as it is, being tender, raw, and young,

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: Which elder days shall ripen and confirm

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: To more approved service and desert.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: I thank thee, gentle Percy; and be sure

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: I count myself in nothing else so happy

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: As in a soul rememb’ring my good friends;

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And as my fortune ripens with thy love,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: It shall be still thy true love’s recompense.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: My heart this covenant makes, my hand thus seals it.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: How far is it to Berkeley, and what stir

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Keeps good old York there with his men of war?

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: There stands the castle by yon tuft of trees,

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: Manned with three hundred men, as I have heard.

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: And in it are the Lords of York, Berkeley, and Seymour,

lines.speaker: PERCY
lines.text: None else of name and noble estimate.
Enter Ross and Willoughby.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Here come the Lords of Ross and Willoughby,

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Bloody with spurring, fiery-red with haste.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Welcome, my lords. I wot your love pursues

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: A banished traitor. All my treasury

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Is yet but unfelt thanks, which, more enriched,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Shall be your love and labour’s recompense.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: Your presence makes us rich, most noble lord.

lines.speaker: WILLOUGHBY
lines.text: And far surmounts our labour to attain it.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Evermore thanks, the exchequer of the poor;

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Which, till my infant fortune comes to years,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Stands for my bounty. But who comes here?
Enter Berkeley.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: It is my Lord of Berkeley, as I guess.

lines.speaker: BERKELEY
lines.text: My Lord of Hereford, my message is to you.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: My lord, my answer is—to “Lancaster”,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And I am come to seek that name in England;

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And I must find that title in your tongue

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Before I make reply to aught you say.

lines.speaker: BERKELEY
lines.text: Mistake me not, my lord, ’tis not my meaning

lines.speaker: BERKELEY
lines.text: To rase one title of your honour out.

lines.speaker: BERKELEY
lines.text: To you, my lord, I come, what lord you will,

lines.speaker: BERKELEY
lines.text: From the most gracious regent of this land,

lines.speaker: BERKELEY
lines.text: The Duke of York, to know what pricks you on

lines.speaker: BERKELEY
lines.text: To take advantage of the absent time,

lines.speaker: BERKELEY
lines.text: And fright our native peace with self-borne arms.
Enter York, attended.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: I shall not need transport my words by you.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Here comes his Grace in person. My noble uncle!
[_Kneels._]

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Show me thy humble heart, and not thy knee,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Whose duty is deceivable and false.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: My gracious uncle—

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Tut, tut!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Grace me no grace, nor uncle me no uncle.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I am no traitor’s uncle, and that word “grace”

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: In an ungracious mouth is but profane.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Why have those banished and forbidden legs

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Dared once to touch a dust of England’s ground?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: But then more why: why have they dared to march

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: So many miles upon her peaceful bosom,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Frighting her pale-faced villages with war

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And ostentation of despised arms?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Com’st thou because the anointed king is hence?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Why, foolish boy, the King is left behind,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And in my loyal bosom lies his power.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Were I but now lord of such hot youth

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: As when brave Gaunt, thy father, and myself

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Rescued the Black Prince, that young Mars of men,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: From forth the ranks of many thousand French,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: O, then how quickly should this arm of mine,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Now prisoner to the palsy, chastise thee

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And minister correction to thy fault!

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: My gracious uncle, let me know my fault.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: On what condition stands it and wherein?

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Even in condition of the worst degree,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: In gross rebellion and detested treason.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Thou art a banished man, and here art come,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Before the expiration of thy time,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: In braving arms against thy sovereign.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: As I was banished, I was banished Hereford;

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: But as I come, I come for Lancaster.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And, noble uncle, I beseech your Grace

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Look on my wrongs with an indifferent eye.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: You are my father, for methinks in you

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: I see old Gaunt alive. O then, my father,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Will you permit that I shall stand condemned

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: A wandering vagabond, my rights and royalties

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Plucked from my arms perforce and given away

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To upstart unthrifts? Wherefore was I born?

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: If that my cousin king be King in England,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: It must be granted I am Duke of Lancaster.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: You have a son, Aumerle, my noble cousin.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Had you first died and he been thus trod down,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: He should have found his uncle Gaunt a father

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To rouse his wrongs and chase them to the bay.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: I am denied to sue my livery here,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And yet my letters patents give me leave.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: My father’s goods are all distrained and sold,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And these, and all, are all amiss employed.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: What would you have me do? I am a subject,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And challenge law. Attorneys are denied me,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And therefore personally I lay my claim

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To my inheritance of free descent.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: The noble Duke hath been too much abused.

lines.speaker: ROSS
lines.text: It stands your Grace upon to do him right.

lines.speaker: WILLOUGHBY
lines.text: Base men by his endowments are made great.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: My lords of England, let me tell you this:

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I have had feeling of my cousin’s wrongs

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And laboured all I could to do him right.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: But in this kind to come, in braving arms,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Be his own carver and cut out his way

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To find out right with wrong, it may not be.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And you that do abet him in this kind

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Cherish rebellion and are rebels all.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: The noble Duke hath sworn his coming is

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: But for his own; and for the right of that

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: We all have strongly sworn to give him aid;

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: And let him never see joy that breaks that oath!

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Well, well, I see the issue of these arms.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I cannot mend it, I must needs confess,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Because my power is weak and all ill-left;

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: But if I could, by Him that gave me life,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I would attach you all and make you stoop

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Unto the sovereign mercy of the King.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: But since I cannot, be it known unto you

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: I do remain as neuter. So fare you well—

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Unless you please to enter in the castle

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And there repose you for this night.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: An offer, uncle, that we will accept;

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: But we must win your Grace to go with us

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To Bristol Castle, which they say is held

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: By Bushy, Bagot, and their complices,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: The caterpillars of the commonwealth,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Which I have sworn to weed and pluck away.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: It may be I will go with you; but yet I’ll pause,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: For I am loath to break our country’s laws.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Nor friends nor foes, to me welcome you are.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Things past redress are now with me past care.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Earl of Salisbury and a Welsh Captain.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: My Lord of Salisbury, we have stayed ten days

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: And hardly kept our countrymen together,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: And yet we hear no tidings from the King.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Therefore we will disperse ourselves. Farewell.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Stay yet another day, thou trusty Welshman.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: The King reposeth all his confidence in thee.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: ’Tis thought the King is dead. We will not stay.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: The bay trees in our country are all withered,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: And meteors fright the fixed stars of heaven;

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: The pale-faced moon looks bloody on the earth,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: And lean-looked prophets whisper fearful change;

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Rich men look sad, and ruffians dance and leap,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: The one in fear to lose what they enjoy,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: The other to enjoy by rage and war.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: These signs forerun the death or fall of kings.

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: Farewell. Our countrymen are gone and fled,

lines.speaker: CAPTAIN
lines.text: As well assured Richard their king is dead.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Ah, Richard! With the eyes of heavy mind

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: I see thy glory like a shooting star

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Fall to the base earth from the firmament.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Thy sun sets weeping in the lowly west,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Witnessing storms to come, woe, and unrest.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Thy friends are fled, to wait upon thy foes,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And crossly to thy good all fortune goes.
[_Exit._]
Enter Bolingbroke, York, Northumberland, Harry Percy, Willoughby, Ross; Officers behind, with Bushy and Green, prisoners.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Bring forth these men.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Bushy and Green, I will not vex your souls—

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Since presently your souls must part your bodies—

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: With too much urging your pernicious lives,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: For ’twere no charity; yet to wash your blood

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: From off my hands, here in the view of men

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: I will unfold some causes of your deaths:

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: You have misled a prince, a royal king,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: A happy gentleman in blood and lineaments,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: By you unhappied and disfigured clean.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: You have in manner with your sinful hours

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Made a divorce betwixt his queen and him,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Broke the possession of a royal bed,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And stained the beauty of a fair queen’s cheeks

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: With tears drawn from her eyes by your foul wrongs.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Myself, a prince by fortune of my birth,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Near to the King in blood, and near in love

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Till you did make him misinterpret me,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Have stooped my neck under your injuries

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And sighed my English breath in foreign clouds,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Eating the bitter bread of banishment,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Whilst you have fed upon my signories,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Disparked my parks and felled my forest woods,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: From my own windows torn my household coat,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Rased out my imprese, leaving me no sign

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Save men’s opinions and my living blood

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To show the world I am a gentleman.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: This and much more, much more than twice all this,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Condemns you to the death. See them delivered over

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To execution and the hand of death.

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: More welcome is the stroke of death to me

lines.speaker: BUSHY
lines.text: Than Bolingbroke to England. Lords, farewell.

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: My comfort is that heaven will take our souls

lines.speaker: GREEN
lines.text: And plague injustice with the pains of hell.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: My Lord Northumberland, see them dispatched.
[_Exeunt Northumberland and Others, with Bushy and Green._]

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Uncle, you say the Queen is at your house;

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: For God’s sake, fairly let her be entreated.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Tell her I send to her my kind commends;

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Take special care my greetings be delivered.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: A gentleman of mine I have dispatched

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: With letters of your love to her at large.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Thanks, gentle uncle. Come, lords, away,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To fight with Glendower and his complices.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: A while to work, and after holiday.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The coast of Wales. A castle in view.

lines.text: Flourish: drums and trumpets. Enter King Richard, the Bishop of Carlisle, Aumerle and soldiers.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Barkloughly Castle call they this at hand?

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Yea, my lord. How brooks your Grace the air

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: After your late tossing on the breaking seas?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Needs must I like it well. I weep for joy

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To stand upon my kingdom once again.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Dear earth, I do salute thee with my hand,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Though rebels wound thee with their horses’ hoofs.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: As a long-parted mother with her child

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Plays fondly with her tears and smiles in meeting,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: So weeping-smiling greet I thee, my earth,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And do thee favours with my royal hands.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Feed not thy sovereign’s foe, my gentle earth,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Nor with thy sweets comfort his ravenous sense,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: But let thy spiders, that suck up thy venom,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And heavy-gaited toads lie in their way,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Doing annoyance to the treacherous feet

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Which with usurping steps do trample thee.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Yield stinging nettles to mine enemies;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And when they from thy bosom pluck a flower,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Guard it, I pray thee, with a lurking adder

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Whose double tongue may with a mortal touch

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Throw death upon thy sovereign’s enemies.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Mock not my senseless conjuration, lords.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: This earth shall have a feeling, and these stones

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Prove armed soldiers, ere her native king

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Shall falter under foul rebellion’s arms.

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Fear not, my lord. That Power that made you king

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Hath power to keep you king in spite of all.

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: The means that heaven yields must be embraced

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: And not neglected; else if heaven would,

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: And we will not. Heaven’s offer we refuse,

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: The proffered means of succour and redress.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: He means, my lord, that we are too remiss,

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Whilst Bolingbroke, through our security,

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Grows strong and great in substance and in power.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Discomfortable cousin, know’st thou not

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: That when the searching eye of heaven is hid

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Behind the globe that lights the lower world,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Then thieves and robbers range abroad unseen

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: In murders and in outrage boldly here;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: But when from under this terrestrial ball

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: He fires the proud tops of the eastern pines

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And darts his light through every guilty hole,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Then murders, treasons, and detested sins,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The cloak of night being plucked from off their backs,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Stand bare and naked, trembling at themselves?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: So when this thief, this traitor, Bolingbroke,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Who all this while hath revelled in the night

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Whilst we were wand’ring with the Antipodes,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Shall see us rising in our throne, the east,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: His treasons will sit blushing in his face,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Not able to endure the sight of day,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: But self-affrighted, tremble at his sin.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Not all the water in the rough rude sea

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Can wash the balm off from an anointed king;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The breath of worldly men cannot depose

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The deputy elected by the Lord.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: For every man that Bolingbroke hath pressed

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To lift shrewd steel against our golden crown,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: God for his Richard hath in heavenly pay

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: A glorious angel. Then, if angels fight,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Weak men must fall, for heaven still guards the right.
Enter Salisbury.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Welcome, my lord. How far off lies your power?

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Nor near nor farther off, my gracious lord,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Than this weak arm. Discomfort guides my tongue

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And bids me speak of nothing but despair.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: One day too late, I fear me, noble lord,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Hath clouded all thy happy days on earth.

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: O, call back yesterday, bid time return,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: And thou shalt have twelve thousand fighting men!

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Today, today, unhappy day, too late,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: O’erthrows thy joys, friends, fortune, and thy state;

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: For all the Welshmen, hearing thou wert dead,

lines.speaker: SALISBURY
lines.text: Are gone to Bolingbroke, dispersed, and fled.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Comfort, my liege. Why looks your Grace so pale?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: But now, the blood of twenty thousand men

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Did triumph in my face, and they are fled;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And till so much blood thither come again

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Have I not reason to look pale and dead?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: All souls that will be safe, fly from my side,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: For time hath set a blot upon my pride.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Comfort, my liege. Remember who you are.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I had forgot myself. Am I not king?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Awake, thou coward majesty! thou sleepest!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Is not the King’s name twenty thousand names?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Arm, arm, my name! A puny subject strikes

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: At thy great glory. Look not to the ground,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Ye favourites of a king. Are we not high?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: High be our thoughts. I know my uncle York

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Hath power enough to serve our turn. But who comes here?
Enter Sir Stephen Scroop.

lines.speaker: SCROOP
lines.text: More health and happiness betide my liege

lines.speaker: SCROOP
lines.text: Than can my care-tuned tongue deliver him.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Mine ear is open and my heart prepared.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: The worst is worldly loss thou canst unfold.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Say, is my kingdom lost? Why, ’twas my care,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: And what loss is it to be rid of care?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Strives Bolingbroke to be as great as we?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Greater he shall not be. If he serve God,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: We’ll serve Him too, and be his fellow so.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Revolt our subjects? That we cannot mend.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: They break their faith to God as well as us.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: As thus, to drop them still upon one place

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Till they have fretted us a pair of graves

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Within the earth; and, therein laid, there lies

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Two kinsmen digged their graves with weeping eyes.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Would not this ill do well? Well, well, I see

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: I talk but idly, and you laugh at me.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Most mighty prince, my Lord Northumberland,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: What says King Bolingbroke? Will his Majesty

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Give Richard leave to live till Richard die?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: You make a leg, and Bolingbroke says ay.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: My lord, in the base court he doth attend

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: To speak with you. May it please you to come down?

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Down, down I come, like glist’ring Phaëthon,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Wanting the manage of unruly jades.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: In the base court? Base court, where kings grow base,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To come at traitors’ calls, and do them grace.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: In the base court? Come down? Down, court! down, king!

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: For night-owls shriek where mounting larks should sing.
[_Exeunt from above._]

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: What says his Majesty?

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Sorrow and grief of heart

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Makes him speak fondly like a frantic man.

lines.speaker: NORTHUMBERLAND
lines.text: Yet he is come.
Enter King Richard and his attendants.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Stand all apart,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And show fair duty to his Majesty.
[_Kneeling_.]

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: My gracious lord.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Fair cousin, you debase your princely knee

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: To make the base earth proud with kissing it.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Me rather had my heart might feel your love

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Than my unpleased eye see your courtesy.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Up, cousin, up. Your heart is up, I know,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Thus high at least, although your knee be low.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: My gracious lord, I come but for mine own.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Your own is yours, and I am yours, and all.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: So far be mine, my most redoubted lord,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: As my true service shall deserve your love.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Well you deserve. They well deserve to have

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: That know the strong’st and surest way to get.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Uncle, give me your hands. Nay, dry your eyes.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Tears show their love, but want their remedies.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Cousin, I am too young to be your father,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Though you are old enough to be my heir.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: What you will have, I’ll give, and willing too;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: For do we must what force will have us do.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Set on towards London, cousin, is it so?

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Yea, my good lord.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Then I must not say no.
[_Flourish. Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: Langley. The Duke of York’s garden.

lines.text: Enter the Queen and two Ladies.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: What sport shall we devise here in this garden

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: To drive away the heavy thought of care?

lines.speaker: LADY
lines.text: Madam, we’ll play at bowls.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: ’Twill make me think the world is full of rubs

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And that my fortune runs against the bias.

lines.speaker: LADY
lines.text: Madam, we’ll dance.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: My legs can keep no measure in delight

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: When my poor heart no measure keeps in grief.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Therefore no dancing, girl; some other sport.

lines.speaker: LADY
lines.text: Madam, we’ll tell tales.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Of sorrow or of joy?

lines.speaker: LADY
lines.text: Of either, madam.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Of neither, girl.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: For if of joy, being altogether wanting,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: It doth remember me the more of sorrow;

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Or if of grief, being altogether had,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: It adds more sorrow to my want of joy.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: For what I have I need not to repeat,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And what I want it boots not to complain.

lines.speaker: LADY
lines.text: Madam, I’ll sing.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: ’Tis well that thou hast cause;

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: But thou shouldst please me better wouldst thou weep.

lines.speaker: LADY
lines.text: I could weep, madam, would it do you good.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And I could sing, would weeping do me good,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And never borrow any tear of thee.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: But stay, here come the gardeners.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Let’s step into the shadow of these trees.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: My wretchedness unto a row of pins,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: They will talk of state, for everyone doth so

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Against a change; woe is forerun with woe.
[_Queen and Ladies retire._]
Enter a Gardener and two Servants.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Go, bind thou up young dangling apricocks,

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Which, like unruly children, make their sire

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Stoop with oppression of their prodigal weight.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Give some supportance to the bending twigs.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Go thou, and like an executioner

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Cut off the heads of too fast-growing sprays

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: That look too lofty in our commonwealth.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: All must be even in our government.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: You thus employed, I will go root away

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: The noisome weeds which without profit suck

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: The soil’s fertility from wholesome flowers.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Why should we in the compass of a pale

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Keep law and form and due proportion,

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Showing, as in a model, our firm estate,

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: When our sea-walled garden, the whole land,

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Is full of weeds, her fairest flowers choked up,

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Her fruit trees all unpruned, her hedges ruined,

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Her knots disordered, and her wholesome herbs

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: Swarming with caterpillars?

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Hold thy peace.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: He that hath suffered this disordered spring

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Hath now himself met with the fall of leaf.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: The weeds which his broad-spreading leaves did shelter,

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: That seemed in eating him to hold him up,

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Are plucked up, root and all, by Bolingbroke—

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: I mean the Earl of Wiltshire, Bushy, Green.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: What, are they dead?

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: They are. And Bolingbroke

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Hath seized the wasteful King. O, what pity is it

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: That he had not so trimmed and dressed his land

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: As we this garden! We at time of year

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Do wound the bark, the skin of our fruit trees,

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Lest, being over-proud in sap and blood,

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: With too much riches it confound itself.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Had he done so to great and growing men,

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: They might have lived to bear and he to taste

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Their fruits of duty. Superfluous branches

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: We lop away, that bearing boughs may live.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Had he done so, himself had home the crown,

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Which waste of idle hours hath quite thrown down.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: What, think you the King shall be deposed?

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Depressed he is already, and deposed

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: ’Tis doubt he will be. Letters came last night

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: To a dear friend of the good Duke of York’s

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: That tell black tidings.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: O, I am pressed to death through want of speaking!
[_Coming forward._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Thou, old Adam’s likeness, set to dress this garden,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: How dares thy harsh rude tongue sound this unpleasing news?

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: What Eve, what serpent, hath suggested thee

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: To make a second fall of cursed man?

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Why dost thou say King Richard is deposed?

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Dar’st thou, thou little better thing than earth,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Divine his downfall? Say, where, when, and how,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Cam’st thou by this ill tidings? Speak, thou wretch!

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Pardon me, madam. Little joy have I

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: To breathe this news; yet what I say is true.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: King Richard, he is in the mighty hold

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Of Bolingbroke. Their fortunes both are weighed.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: In your lord’s scale is nothing but himself,

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: And some few vanities that make him light;

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: But in the balance of great Bolingbroke,

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Besides himself, are all the English peers,

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: And with that odds he weighs King Richard down.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Post you to London, and you will find it so.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: I speak no more than everyone doth know.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Nimble mischance, that art so light of foot,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Doth not thy embassage belong to me,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: And am I last that knows it? O, thou thinkest

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: To serve me last that I may longest keep

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Thy sorrow in my breast. Come, ladies, go

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: To meet at London London’s king in woe.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: What, was I born to this, that my sad look

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Should grace the triumph of great Bolingbroke?

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Gard’ner, for telling me these news of woe,

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Pray God the plants thou graft’st may never grow!
[_Exeunt Queen and Ladies._]

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Poor Queen, so that thy state might be no worse,

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: I would my skill were subject to thy curse.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Here did she fall a tear. Here in this place

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: I’ll set a bank of rue, sour herb of grace.

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: Rue even for ruth here shortly shall be seen

lines.speaker: GARDENER
lines.text: In the remembrance of a weeping queen.
[_Exeunt._]

The Lords spiritual on the right side of the throne; the Lords temporal on the left; the Commons below. Enter Bolingbroke, Aumerle, Surrey, Northumberland, Harry Percy, Fitzwater, another Lord, the Bishop of Carlisle, the Abbot of Westminster and attendants.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Call forth Bagot.
Enter Officers with Bagot.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Now, Bagot, freely speak thy mind,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: What thou dost know of noble Gloucester’s death,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Who wrought it with the King, and who performed

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: The bloody office of his timeless end.

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: Then set before my face the Lord Aumerle.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Cousin, stand forth, and look upon that man.

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: My Lord Aumerle, I know your daring tongue

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: Scorns to unsay what once it hath delivered.

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: In that dead time when Gloucester’s death was plotted,

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: I heard you say “Is not my arm of length,

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: That reacheth from the restful English Court

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: As far as Calais, to mine uncle’s head?”

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: Amongst much other talk that very time

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: I heard you say that you had rather refuse

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: The offer of an hundred thousand crowns

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: Than Bolingbroke’s return to England,

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: Adding withal, how blest this land would be

lines.speaker: BAGOT
lines.text: In this your cousin’s death.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Princes and noble lords,

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: What answer shall I make to this base man?

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Shall I so much dishonour my fair stars

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: On equal terms to give him chastisement?

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Either I must, or have mine honour soiled

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: With the attainder of his slanderous lips.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: There is my gage, the manual seal of death

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: That marks thee out for hell. I say thou liest,

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: And will maintain what thou hast said is false

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: In thy heart-blood, though being all too base

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: To stain the temper of my knightly sword.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Bagot, forbear. Thou shalt not take it up.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Excepting one, I would he were the best

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: In all this presence that hath moved me so.

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: If that thy valour stand on sympathy,

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: There is my gage, Aumerle, in gage to thine.

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: By that fair sun which shows me where thou stand’st,

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: I heard thee say, and vauntingly thou spak’st it,

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: That thou wert cause of noble Gloucester’s death.

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: If thou deniest it twenty times, thou liest!

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: And I will turn thy falsehood to thy heart,

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: Where it was forged, with my rapier’s point.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Thou dar’st not, coward, live to see that day.

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: Now, by my soul, I would it were this hour.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Fitzwater, thou art damned to hell for this.

lines.speaker: HARRY PERCY
lines.text: Aumerle, thou liest. His honour is as true

lines.speaker: HARRY PERCY
lines.text: In this appeal as thou art an unjust;

lines.speaker: HARRY PERCY
lines.text: And that thou art so, there I throw my gage,

lines.speaker: HARRY PERCY
lines.text: To prove it on thee to the extremest point

lines.speaker: HARRY PERCY
lines.text: Of mortal breathing. Seize it if thou dar’st.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: And if I do not, may my hands rot off

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: And never brandish more revengeful steel

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Over the glittering helmet of my foe!

lines.speaker: ANOTHER LORD
lines.text: I task the earth to the like, forsworn Aumerle,

lines.speaker: ANOTHER LORD
lines.text: And spur thee on with full as many lies

lines.speaker: ANOTHER LORD
lines.text: As may be holloaed in thy treacherous ear

lines.speaker: ANOTHER LORD
lines.text: From sun to sun. There is my honour’s pawn.

lines.speaker: ANOTHER LORD
lines.text: Engage it to the trial if thou dar’st.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Who sets me else? By heaven, I’ll throw at all.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: I have a thousand spirits in one breast

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: To answer twenty thousand such as you.

lines.speaker: SURREY
lines.text: My Lord Fitzwater, I do remember well

lines.speaker: SURREY
lines.text: The very time Aumerle and you did talk.

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: ’Tis very true. You were in presence then,

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: And you can witness with me this is true.

lines.speaker: SURREY
lines.text: As false, by heaven, as heaven itself is true.

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: Surrey, thou liest.

lines.speaker: SURREY
lines.text: Dishonourable boy!

lines.speaker: SURREY
lines.text: That lie shall lie so heavy on my sword

lines.speaker: SURREY
lines.text: That it shall render vengeance and revenge

lines.speaker: SURREY
lines.text: Till thou the lie-giver and that lie do lie

lines.speaker: SURREY
lines.text: In earth as quiet as thy father’s skull.

lines.speaker: SURREY
lines.text: In proof whereof, there is my honour’s pawn.

lines.speaker: SURREY
lines.text: Engage it to the trial if thou dar’st.

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: How fondly dost thou spur a forward horse!

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: If I dare eat, or drink, or breathe, or live,

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: I dare meet Surrey in a wilderness

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: And spit upon him, whilst I say he lies,

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: And lies, and lies. There is my bond of faith

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: To tie thee to my strong correction.

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: As I intend to thrive in this new world,

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: Aumerle is guilty of my true appeal.

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: Besides, I heard the banished Norfolk say

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: That thou, Aumerle, didst send two of thy men

lines.speaker: FITZWATER
lines.text: To execute the noble duke at Calais.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Some honest Christian trust me with a gage.

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: That Norfolk lies, here do I throw down this,

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: If he may be repealed to try his honour.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: These differences shall all rest under gage

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Till Norfolk be repealed. Repealed he shall be,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: And, though mine enemy, restored again

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: To all his lands and signories. When he is returned,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Against Aumerle we will enforce his trial.

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: That honourable day shall ne’er be seen.

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Many a time hath banished Norfolk fought

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: For Jesu Christ in glorious Christian field,

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Streaming the ensign of the Christian cross

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Against black pagans, Turks, and Saracens;

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: And, toiled with works of war, retired himself

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: To Italy, and there at Venice gave

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: His body to that pleasant country’s earth

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: And his pure soul unto his captain, Christ,

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Under whose colours he had fought so long.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Why, Bishop, is Norfolk dead?

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: As surely as I live, my lord.

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Sweet peace conduct his sweet soul to the bosom

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Of good old Abraham! Lords appellants,

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Your differences shall all rest under gage

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: Till we assign you to your days of trial.
Enter York, attended.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Great Duke of Lancaster, I come to thee

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: From plume-plucked Richard, who with willing soul

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Adopts thee heir, and his high sceptre yields

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: To the possession of thy royal hand.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Ascend his throne, descending now from him,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And long live Henry, of that name the fourth!

lines.speaker: BOLINGBROKE
lines.text: In God’s name, I’ll ascend the regal throne.

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Marry, God forbid!

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Worst in this royal presence may I speak,

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Yet best beseeming me to speak the truth.

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Would God that any in this noble presence

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Were enough noble to be upright judge

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Of noble Richard! Then true noblesse would

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Learn him forbearance from so foul a wrong.

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: What subject can give sentence on his king?

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: And who sits here that is not Richard’s subject?

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Thieves are not judged but they are by to hear,

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Although apparent guilt be seen in them;

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: And shall the figure of God’s majesty,

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: His captain, steward, deputy elect,

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Anointed, crowned, planted many years,

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Be judged by subject and inferior breath,

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: And he himself not present? O, forfend it, God,

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: That in a Christian climate souls refined

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Should show so heinous, black, obscene a deed!

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: I speak to subjects, and a subject speaks,

lines.speaker: CARLISLE
lines.text: Stirred up by God, thus boldly for his king.

lines.speaker: CARLISLE

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Go, count thy way with sighs, I mine with groans.

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: So longest way shall have the longest moans.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Come, come, in wooing sorrow let’s be brief,

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: One kiss shall stop our mouths, and dumbly part;

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Thus give I mine, and thus take I thy heart.
[_They kiss._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: Give me mine own again; ’twere no good part

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: To take on me to keep and kill thy heart.
[_They kiss again._]

lines.speaker: QUEEN

lines.speaker: QUEEN
lines.text: That I may strive to kill it with a groan.

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD

lines.speaker: KING RICHARD
lines.text: Once more, adieu. The rest let sorrow say.
[_Exeunt._]

scenes.setting: The same. A room in the Duke of York’s palace.

lines.text: His face still combating with tears and smiles,

lines.text: The badges of his grief and patience,

lines.text: That had not God for some strong purpose, steeled

lines.text: The hearts of men, they must perforce have melted,

lines.text: And barbarism itself have pitied him.

lines.text: Welcome, my son. Who are the violets now

lines.text: That strew the green lap of the new-come spring?

lines.text: Madam, I know not, nor I greatly care not.

lines.text: God knows I had as lief be none as one.

[_To Servant_.]

lines.text: He is as like thee as a man may be,

lines.speaker: YORK

[_Exit._]

lines.text: I’ll not be long behind. Though I be old,

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: And never will I rise up from the ground

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: Till Bolingbroke have pardoned thee. Away, be gone!

scenes.setting: Windsor. A room in the Castle.

lines.text: Enter Bolingbroke as King, Harry Percy and other Lords.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Can no man tell me of my unthrifty son?

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: ’Tis full three months since I did see him last.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: If any plague hang over us, ’tis he.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: I would to God, my lords, he might be found.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Inquire at London, ’mongst the taverns there,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: For there, they say, he daily doth frequent

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: With unrestrained loose companions,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Even such, they say, as stand in narrow lanes

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And beat our watch and rob our passengers,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: While he, young wanton and effeminate boy,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Takes on the point of honour to support

lines.text: So dissolute a crew.

lines.text: My lord, some two days since I saw the Prince,

lines.text: And what said the gallant?

lines.text: And wear it as a favour, and with that

lines.text: As dissolute as desperate! Yet through both

lines.text: I see some sparks of better hope, which elder years

lines.text: May happily bring forth. But who comes here?
Enter Aumerle.

lines.text: Where is the King?

lines.text: What means our cousin that he stares and looks so wildly?

lines.text: God save your Grace! I do beseech your majesty

lines.text: To have some conference with your Grace alone.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Withdraw yourselves, and leave us here alone.
[_Exeunt Harry Percy and Lords._]

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: What is the matter with our cousin now?
[_Kneels_.]

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: For ever may my knees grow to the earth,

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: My tongue cleave to my roof within my mouth,

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Unless a pardon ere I rise or speak.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Intended or committed was this fault?

lines.text: If on the first, how heinous e’er it be,

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: Then give me leave that I may turn the key,

lines.speaker: AUMERLE
lines.text: That no man enter till my tale be done.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Have thy desire.
[_Aumerle locks the door._]
[_Within_.]

lines.text: My liege, beware! Look to thyself!

[_Within_.]

lines.text: Open the door, secure, foolhardy king!

lines.text: Shall I for love speak treason to thy face?

lines.text: Open the door, or I will break it open.

Enter York.

lines.text: What is the matter, uncle? Speak!

lines.text: It was, villain, ere thy hand did set it down.

lines.text: I tore it from the traitor’s bosom, king.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Fear, and not love, begets his penitence.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Forget to pity him, lest thy pity prove

lines.text: A serpent that will sting thee to the heart.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O heinous, strong, and bold conspiracy!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: O loyal father of a treacherous son!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thou sheer, immaculate, and silver fountain

lines.text: From whence this stream through muddy passages

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Hath held his current and defiled himself!

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Thy overflow of good converts to bad,

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: And thy abundant goodness shall excuse

lines.text: This deadly blot in thy digressing son.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: So shall my virtue be his vice’s bawd,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: And he shall spend mine honour with his shame,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: As thriftless sons their scraping fathers’ gold.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Mine honour lives when his dishonour dies,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Or my shamed life in his dishonour lies.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: Thou kill’st me in his life: giving him breath,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: The traitor lives, the true man’s put to death.
[_Within_.]

lines.text: What ho, my liege! For God’s sake, let me in!

lines.text: What shrill-voiced suppliant makes this eager cry?
[_Within_.]

lines.text: A woman, and thine aunt, great king, ’tis I.

lines.text: Speak with me, pity me, open the door!

lines.speaker: DUCHESS
lines.text: A beggar begs that never begged before.

lines.text: My dangerous cousin, let your mother in.

lines.text: I know she’s come to pray for your foul sin.
Enter Duchess.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: If thou do pardon whosoever pray,

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: More sins for this forgiveness prosper may.

lines.speaker: YORK
lines.text: This festered joint cut off, the rest rest sound;

lines.text: This let alone will all the rest confound.

lines.text: O King, believe not this hard-hearted man.

lines.text: Love loving not itself none other can.

lines.text: Thou frantic woman, what dost thou make here?

lines.text: Shall thy old dugs once more a traitor rear?

lines.text: Sweet York, be patient. [_Kneels_.] Hear me, gentle liege.

lines.text: Rise up, good aunt.

lines.text: For ever will I walk upon my knees

lines.text: Till thou give joy, until thou bid me joy

lines.text: By pardoning Rutland, my transgressing boy.

[_Kneels._]

lines.text: Against them both, my true joints bended be.

lines.text: Ill mayst thou thrive if thou grant any grace!

lines.text: Pleads he in earnest? Look upon his face.

lines.text: His eyes do drop no tears, his prayers are in jest;

lines.text: His words come from his mouth, ours from our breast.

lines.text: He prays but faintly and would be denied;

lines.text: We pray with heart and soul and all beside:

lines.text: Dost thou teach pardon pardon to destroy?

lines.text: Ah! my sour husband, my hard-hearted lord,

lines.text: Good aunt, stand up.

lines.text: With all my heart

lines.text: To Oxford, or where’er these traitors are;

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: They shall not live within this world, I swear,

lines.text: But I will have them, if I once know where.

lines.speaker: KING HENRY
lines.text: Uncle, farewell, and cousin, adieu.

lines.text: Your mother well hath prayed, and prove you true.
